title: Verifier-Assisted versus LLM-Only Pre-deployment Network-Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measure whether integrating a deterministic pre-deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent-driven network-change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single-shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre-deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by superficial syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern is to pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the single-shot quality of the generator, the validator's expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) designed to isolate the deterministic rescue attributable to post-generation validation and a bounded repair operator while conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (the shared_initial estimand). For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re-validated. The central research question is: under the shared_initial estimand, does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre-deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-archived paired evaluation that isolates bounded deterministic rescue applied to a single LLM draw per intent. (2) A complete execution and analysis bundle (preregistration, task manifests, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis) with transparent inferential reporting. (3) An evidence-grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, estimand conditioning, validator coverage, and operational implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document active LLM applications in NetOps including intent translation, template synthesis, automated test-case generation, and repair, and they emphasize the importance of semantic correctness beyond syntactic validity [1–3]. Tool-augmented, planner-centric, and ReAct-style frameworks enable LLMs to call external validators and simulators, decomposing multi-step NetOps workflows and coordinating tool outputs; such frameworks motivate empirical study of verifier-augmentation patterns [4,5]. Empirical reports indicate that generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains depend strongly on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether evaluations permit resampling or iterative regeneration [5,3].

Work addressing hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets highlights detectors and retrieval/self-reflection methods to reduce semantic errors, but transfer to complex NetOps semantics depends on validator expressiveness and threat models [6]. Separate research on formal or hybrid repair (symbolic fault localization combined with generative repair operators) shows promise for certain fault classes but also exposes integration complexity and variance across benchmarks [7,8]. These threads motivate our design decisions: a focused estimand definition (shared_initial), a constrained repair budget to bound model-call costs, and explicit semantic validation tied to topology and sequencing invariants encoded in the synthetic benchmark.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The full confirmatory design was preregistered under study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier-pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents, analyzed per the preregistered paired executor (exact McNemar two-sided test) and accompanied by a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination controls, the analysis executor, multiplicity handling for exploratory strata tests, and the repair budget (≤1 automated repair per pair). The preregistered optional pilot for discordance estimation was not executed; no post-preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were produced deterministically by an archived generator into a synthetic_topology_suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task manifest encodes the natural-language intent, initial and expected final device states, required sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership; the confirmatory main run sampled 100 pairs per stratum for a total of 300 pairs.

Shared_initial production and model configuration. To isolate deterministic verifier/repair rescue from resampling benefits we implemented the shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate which was used verbatim in both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator for shared_initial production was gpt-5-mini run with minimal reasoning effort and an output-token cap sufficient for configuration fragments. Reusing the identical candidate across conditions prevents differences due to independent additional model draws and bounds the estimand to post-generation validation and bounded repair on a single draw.

Deterministic validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: it deterministically checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and protected-interface templates. Scoring is binary for the estimand: an unflagged candidate constitutes a pass. The guarded pipeline permits at most one automated repair (repair budget ≤1). The repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (for example, inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). Repair attempts are applied only to flagged shared_initial candidates and are deterministically re-validated. Repair candidates that remain flagged after the single permitted edit count as failures for the guarded condition in the primary analysis.

Contamination controls and missingness. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection (negative controls and invariant checks). Pairs would be excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls for that pair failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; if only a single call failed the pair would be retained per the executor's complete_pair_primary rule, with a sensitivity analysis that treats single-call failures as failures. All provider/API failures and exclusion reasons were logged.

Inferential procedures. The confirmatory analysis computed the 2×2 paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline), an exact two-sided McNemar test on discordant counts, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). Secondary exploratory analyses (per-stratum tests) were labeled exploratory and subjected to multiplicity control when reported. All analysis code and seeds were archived and executed as preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution integrity and accounting. The preregistered adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 producing complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Model-call accounting recorded 301 model calls (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation). Instrumentation confirmed that the shared_initial candidate was reused across baseline and guarded conditions and that deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1) the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per-stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Stratified tallies were: low difficulty baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. All discordance is concentrated in the high stratum (one guarded-only rescue). The solitary discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair: the validator flagged a sequencing omission (a missing explicit 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained edit operator performed a single insertion of the missing sequencing command and the validator reported success after the edit. Thus the single deterministic rescue required one repair invocation.

Contamination and missingness outcome. Contamination checks did not flag anomalies. No pairs were excluded under the preregistered rules; there were zero failed or unscorable episodes in either condition in the confirmatory dataset.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue required a single additional repair-stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating negligible marginal model-call cost for bounded repair in this run. The empirical repair_stage_count = 1 quantifies the low marginal runtime/model cost for deterministic rescue under the chosen repair budget and edit operator design.

Statistical interpretation. The observed p = 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant pairs under the shared_initial estimand and the synthetic suite's near-ceiling baseline. Exact McNemar inference depends only on n10 and n01; with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 the two-sided exact p equals 1.0, indicating no statistically detectable difference under conventional two-sided testing in this sample. The paired bootstrap CI provides a complementary bound: the absolute paired improvement is plausibly between 0 and 0.01 given observed data and the preregistered estimand. These inferential claims apply strictly to the shared_initial conditioning, the limited repair budget (≤1 constrained edit), the synthetic task distribution, and the declared generator and validator.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent corresponds to operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier-guided regeneration, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows should be evaluated under different preregistered estimands that permit additional model calls.

Ceiling effects and the omitted pilot. The preregistration targeted detection of a larger absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on a pilot to estimate discordance. Because the optional pilot was not executed the main run encountered a near-ceiling baseline (299/300), producing only one discordant observation and reducing sensitivity to small absolute differences. This practical outcome emphasizes the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on chosen task suites.

Validator coverage and failure-mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) did not appear at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that detect reachability or complex ACL semantics may increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, if operator policy disallows automated edits, a guarded pipeline's immediate operational value reduces to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget and design tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue and to quantify marginal model-call cost. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or verifier-guided regeneration would expand rescue opportunities but address a different estimand and incur greater model-call cost. The archived single repair trace permits forensic evaluation of the edit's semantics and can inform acceptable edit-operator design in production CI/CD.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational choices: if pipelines permit multiple model calls or verifier-guided regeneration, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering to measure achievable success rates under those policies. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides a conservative operational bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. In this run bounded repair produced a deterministic rescue in one hard example with negligible additional model-call expenditure; in other task distributions the tradeoff between repair budget and model-call cost will differ.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-archived paired comparison between a verifier-assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single-shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Baseline single-shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near-ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and to enable follow-up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, validator expressiveness, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real-world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or to richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single-shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre-specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post-preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
